# 1 Clement Chapter 59 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 59 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_059_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 59

*[The Great Prayer — Part I: Opening Address and Petition for Illumination]*

**59:1** But if there be any who are disobedient to what has been said by him through us, let them know that they will enmesh themselves in transgression and no small peril; but as for us, we shall be innocent of this sin, and we will pray with earnest entreaty and supplication that the Creator of all things may keep intact the full number of his elect throughout the whole world, through his beloved servant Jesus Christ, through whom he called us from darkness to light, from ignorance to the full knowledge of the glory of his name.

**59:2** Grant us, Lord, to set our hope upon your name, which is the primal source of all creation; open the eyes of our hearts to know you, the only Highest in the highest, the Holy One resting among the holy; you who bring low the pride of the arrogant, who scatter the purposes of nations, who lift up the lowly and abase the lofty; you who make rich and make poor; you who kill and make alive, the sole Finder of spirits and the God of all flesh; you who look upon the depths and observe the works of men; the Succourer of those who are in peril, the Savior of those who have despaired, the Creator and Guardian of every spirit; you who multiply the nations upon the earth and from all have chosen those who love you through Jesus Christ, your beloved servant — through whom you have instructed us, hallowed us, and honored us.

**59:3** We beseech you, Master: be our helper and champion. Those among us who are in affliction — save them; those who are humbled — raise them up; those who have fallen — lift them up; those who are sick — heal them; those who wander from your people — turn them back; those who hunger — feed them; those who are bound — release them; those who are weak — strengthen them; those who are despondent — give courage. Let all the nations know you, that you alone are God, and that Jesus Christ is your servant, and we are your people and the sheep of your pasture.

---

*LOGOS renders according to the standard Greek text of Codex Alexandrinus with attention to formal correspondence. The Great Prayer (chs. 59–61) is rendered with elevated liturgical register.*
